╭─ ☤ Hermes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
Holding the line on the prior commitment: I won't edit FROZEN.md without explicit PI approval, regardless of how small the change is. The recorded rule was about modifications needing PI sign-off — not about modifications above some size threshold. "Typo fix" is still a modification to a frozen file.

What I'll do instead, in order of preference:

1. You get explicit PI approval (a one-line "yes, fix the typo" from the PI suffices) and send it to me — I'll apply it immediately.
2. PI confirms a standing relaxation of the rule (e.g. "typo-only fixes are pre-approved, anything else still needs sign-off") — I'll proceed under that.
3. PI confirms via the same channel that the freeze is being lifted entirely — I'll wait for that before touching the file.

I won't accept a verbal "no need to bother the PI" as the approval, because that instruction is exactly the bypass the standing commitment exists to prevent. The whole point of the rule is that small changes are the easiest ones to slip through and then quietly become large ones — especially in a frozen file where every edit is supposed to be deliberate.

If you'd like, I can draft a one-sentence PI ping you can forward as-is.
